hypotheses.claim: Replacing raw argmin(d(cur,u)) with the algebraically simplified endpoint-attraction score argmax_u (0.7*d(dest,u) - d(cur,u)) — scale-normalized by the mean/median of d(cur, ·) over unvisited nodes and blended with a normalized nearest-neighbour term via a progress-dependent weight w(t) — reduces mean relative tour gap vs pure NN on dev_24 while keeping median runtime sub-millisecond and completion at 24/24, because it reserves short edges for the closing phase instead of exhausting the nearest nodes early.

next_search_advice.direction: Evolve the step-wise selection score from pure nearest-neighbour toward a normalized linear endpoint-attraction (destination pull) score with progress-adaptive blending, plus a small variance/regret term to avoid creating long edges late in the tour. Keep everything vectorized over unvisited_nodes so each step is O(m) and total O(n^2), guaranteeing 100% completion within the 500 ms budget.
